title: Curry’s Ankle‑Breaker on Luka Powers Warriors’ Epic 25‑Point Comeback Victory
body:
The Golden State Warriors erased a 25‑point deficit in the fourth quarter on Friday night, pulling off a 112‑95 triumph over the Los Angeles Lakers thanks to a dazzling 31‑point surge from Stephen Curry that included a dramatic ankle‑breaker move on Luka Doncic‑style flair. The comeback, the largest fourth‑quarter rally in Warriors franchise history, not only re‑energized a struggling Golden State squad but also sent a clear message to Western Conference rivals that the team remains a formidable contender despite early‑season turbulence.

From the opening tip, the Lakers seized control, building a 30‑point lead midway through the third quarter on the back of strong interior play from Anthony Davis and efficient shooting from LeBron James. By the time the Warriors finally found rhythm, the scoreboard read 78‑53 in favor of Los Angeles, and many in the arena began to assume the game was effectively over. Yet the Golden State bench, led by veteran point guard Chris Paul and sharpshooter Klay Thompson, began to chip away at the margin with timely three‑pointers and aggressive defense that forced the Lakers into a series of turnovers.

The turning point arrived early in the fourth quarter when Curry, having struggled to find his usual flow early in the night, ignited a scoring avalanche. After a swift pick‑and‑roll with Draymond Green, Curry drove to the basket, spun past a sliding defender, and launched a step‑back three that swished cleanly. The move, reminiscent of Luka Doncic’s signature ankle‑breaker, left the crowd roaring and seemed to unlock the Warriors’ offensive engine. Curry proceeded to score on 12 of his next 14 attempts, mixing deep threes, mid‑range jumpers and aggressive drives to the rim, while also dishing out five assists that sparked secondary scoring from Andrew Wiggins and Jonathan Kuhn.

Beyond Curry’s heroics, the Warriors’ resurgence was a collective effort. Green’s defensive intensity forced the Lakers into a 12‑0 run that shifted momentum, while the bench contributed 28 points, with Jordan Poole delivering a crucial three‑pointer that extended the lead to 101‑95 with just under three minutes remaining. The Lakers, meanwhile, appeared to lose composure; James, who had amassed 28 points and 10 rebounds, missed several key free throws in the final stretch, and Davis struggled to assert his presence in the paint as the Warriors’ perimeter pressure intensified.

Analysts will likely point to this game as a litmus test for both franchises. For Golden State, the win demonstrates that the roster’s depth and Curry’s elite scoring ability can overcome early deficits, a quality that will be essential as the Western Conference tightens. The performance also bodes well for the team’s chemistry, suggesting that the integration of new pieces—most notably Paul’s veteran leadership—has begun to click. Conversely, the Lakers’ inability to maintain a sizable lead raises concerns about defensive cohesion and late‑game execution, especially as they aim to solidify a playoff spot in a crowded field.

Looking ahead, the Warriors will travel to Denver for their next matchup, where they will test their newfound momentum against a high‑altitude, defensively disciplined opponent. If Curry can replicate his late‑night fireworks and the supporting cast continues to deliver, Golden State could re‑establish itself as a top seed contender. Meanwhile, the Lakers must regroup quickly, addressing their fourth‑quarter lapses and tightening defensive rotations if they hope to stay within striking distance of the postseason. The dramatic comeback in San Francisco serves as a reminder that in the NBA, no lead is safe and every game can pivot on a single, electrifying moment.
